sentences.zh: 郭太字林宗，

translations.literal: Guo Tai, style name Linzong,
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai, whose courtesy name was Linzong,

sentences.zh: 〈范曄父名泰，故改爲此「太」。

translations.literal: (Fan Ye's father was named Tai, so [the text] was changed to this character "tai".
translations.idiomatic: (Because Fan Ye's father was named Tai, the historian renders the name with this character "tai" instead.

sentences.zh: 鄭公業之名亦同焉。〉

translations.literal: Zheng Gongye's name was handled in the same way.)
translations.idiomatic: The same substitution applies to the name of Zheng Gongye.)

sentences.zh: 太原界休人也。

translations.literal: He was a man of Jieqiu in Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He came from Jieqiu in Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈介休，今汾州縣。〉

translations.literal: (Jieqiu is now Fenzhou county.)
translations.idiomatic: (Present-day Jieqiu is Fenzhou county.)

sentences.zh: 家世貧賤。

translations.literal: His family background was poor and lowly.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and of humble station.

sentences.zh: 早孤，母欲使給事縣廷。

translations.literal: He was orphaned early; his mother wished to have him serve in the county yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while still young, he was to be put to clerking in the county offices—his mother's plan.

sentences.zh: 〈《蒼頡篇》曰：「廷，直也。

translations.literal: (The Cangjie Pian says: "ting means straight.
translations.idiomatic: (The Cangjie Pian glosses the graph: "ting means straight.

sentences.zh: 」《說文》：「廷，朝中也。

translations.literal: "The Shuowen: "ting means in the midst of court.
translations.idiomatic: "The Shuowen defines it: "ting is the court's center.

sentences.zh: 」《風俗通》：「廷，正也。

translations.literal: "The Fengsu Tong: "ting means correct.
translations.idiomatic: "The Fengsu Tong adds: "ting means upright.

sentences.zh: 言縣廷、郡廷、朝廷，皆取平均正直也。」〉

translations.literal: Speaking of county yamen, commandery yamen, and court—all take the sense of even, straight, and upright.")
translations.idiomatic: Thus countyting, commanderyting, and courtting all invoke fairness and rectitude.")

sentences.zh: 林宗曰：「大丈夫焉能處斗筲之役乎？

translations.literal: Linzong said: "How can a great man occupy the service of a peck-and-dipper's measure?
translations.idiomatic: Linzong replied: "Would a man of stature tie himself to mean clerk's work—fit for a peck basket and dipper?

sentences.zh: 」遂辭。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he declined.
translations.idiomatic: "—and refused the post.

sentences.zh: 就成皐屈伯彥學，三年業畢，博通墳籍。

translations.literal: He then studied with Qu Boyan of Chenggao; after three years his course was finished, and he was broadly conversant with the canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Chenggao to study under Qu Boyan; three years later he had mastered the curriculum and could move fluently through the classics.

sentences.zh: 善談論，美音制。

translations.literal: He was skilled in discussion and had a fine voice and deportment.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at discourse, and his voice and bearing commanded attention.

sentences.zh: 乃游於洛陽。

translations.literal: He then travelled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He set out for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 始見河南尹李膺，膺大竒之，遂相友善，於是名震京師。

translations.literal: When he first met Commandant of Henan Li Ying, Ying thought him extraordinary; they became close friends, and thereafter his name shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On his first meeting with Li Ying, the governor of Henan, Ying saw something remarkable in him; the two became fast friends, and Guo Tai's name soon resounded through the capital.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，衣冠諸儒送至河上，車數千兩。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home district; the gentry and scholars escorted him to the river—several thousand carriages.
translations.idiomatic: When he went home, gowned scholars turned out in force to see him to the river—thousands of carriages lined the way.

sentences.zh: 林宗唯與李膺同舟而濟，衆賔望之，以爲神仙焉。

translations.literal: Linzong alone crossed in one boat with Li Ying; the assembled guests gazed after them and thought them immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Linzong alone boarded a boat with Li Ying; the crowd on the bank watched the pair cross as if they were watching immortals.

sentences.zh: 司徒黃瓊辟，太常趙典舉有道。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Huang Qiong summoned him; Minister of Ceremonies Zhao Dian recommended him as "worthy of the Way".
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qiong, the Minister of Education, offered him appointment; Zhao Dian, the Minister of Ceremonies, nominated him as a man "worthy of the Way."

sentences.zh: 或勸林宗仕進者，對曰：「吾夜觀乾象，晝察人事，天之所廢，不可支也。」

translations.literal: When some urged Linzong to take office, he replied: "I observe the patterns of heaven by night and human affairs by day; what Heaven casts off cannot be propped up."
translations.idiomatic: To those who urged him into office he said: "At night I read the sky; by day I read the world. What Heaven has cast aside no man can shore up."

sentences.zh: 〈《左傳》晉汝叔寬之詞。

translations.literal: (These are the words of Jin's Ru Shukuan in the Zuo Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: (The line echoes Ru Shukuan of Jin in the Zuo Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 支猶持也。〉

translations.literal: zhi here means to support.)
translations.idiomatic: Here zhi means to prop or sustain.)

sentences.zh: 遂並不應。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not respond to either.
translations.idiomatic: He declined both summonses.

sentences.zh: 性明知人，好獎訓士類。

translations.literal: By nature he was perceptive in judging men and fond of encouraging and instructing scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for reading character, and he took pleasure in lifting up and guiding other scholars.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，容貌魁偉，襃衣博帶，周遊郡國。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi tall, with a commanding appearance; in loose robes and broad sashes he travelled through the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi in height, imposing in build, he wore ample robes and wide belts as he moved from one commandery to the next.

sentences.zh: 甞於陳梁閒行遇雨，巾一角墊，

translations.literal: Once, walking between Chen and Liang, he was caught in the rain; one corner of his headcloth was turned up (folded up).
translations.idiomatic: Walking once between Chen and Liang in a downpour, he folded one corner of his headcloth upward—

sentences.zh: 〈音丁念反。

translations.literal: (Pronounced with the ding-nian fanqie.
translations.idiomatic: (Reading: ding-nian fanqie.

sentences.zh: 周遷《輿服雜事》曰：「巾以葛爲之，形如幍，音口洽反。

translations.literal: Zhou Qian's Miscellany on Carriages and Dress says: "The headcloth is made of kudzu fiber, shaped like a zhao, pronounced kou-qia fanqie.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qian's notes on dress describe the headcloth as kudzu, cap-shaped (zhao), glossed kou-qia.

sentences.zh: 本居士野人所服。

translations.literal: Originally it was what recluses and rustics wore.
translations.idiomatic: Rustic scholars and countrymen had worn it first.

sentences.zh: 魏武造幍，其巾乃廢。

translations.literal: When Wei Wu [Cao Cao] created the zhao, this headcloth then fell out of use.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao of Wei introduced the formal zhao cap, the old headcloth went out of fashion.

sentences.zh: 今國子學生服焉。

translations.literal: Now students of the Imperial Academy wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Students at the Imperial Academy wear it today.

sentences.zh: 以白紗爲之。」〉

translations.literal: It is made of white gauze.")
translations.idiomatic: The cap is white gauze.")

sentences.zh: 時人乃故折巾一角，以爲「林宗巾」。

translations.literal: People of the time then deliberately folded one corner of the headcloth, calling it the "Linzong headcloth".
translations.idiomatic: Fashion followed: men deliberately cocked one corner of the headcloth and called the style the "Linzong fold."

sentences.zh: 其見慕皆如此。

translations.literal: The degree to which he was admired was all like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the admiration he inspired.

sentences.zh: 〈泰別傳曰：「泰名顯，士爭歸之，載刺常盈車。」〉

translations.literal: (Tai's separate biography says: "Tai's name was manifest; scholars vied to attach themselves to him; visiting cards loaded on carts were always full.")
translations.idiomatic: (A separate biography of Guo Tai notes that his reputation drew scholars in crowds—visiting cards piled until the carts overflowed.)

sentences.zh: 或問汝南范滂曰：「郭林宗何如人？

translations.literal: Someone asked Fan Pang of Runan: "What sort of man is Guo Linzong?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Pang of Runan was once asked, "What kind of man is Guo Linzong?

sentences.zh: 」滂曰：「隱不違親，

translations.literal: "Pang said: "In reclusion he does not violate kinship,
translations.idiomatic: "Pang answered: "In withdrawal he does not wrong his parents—

sentences.zh: 〈介推之類。〉

translations.literal: (The type of Jie Tui.)
translations.idiomatic: (like Jie Zhitui.)

sentences.zh: 貞不絕俗，

translations.literal: In integrity he does not cut himself off from the world,
translations.idiomatic: In integrity he does not turn his back on the world—

sentences.zh: 〈柳下惠之類。〉

translations.literal: (The type of Liuxia Hui.)
translations.idiomatic: (like Liuxia Hui.)

sentences.zh: 天子不得臣，諸侯不得友，吾不知其它。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven cannot make him a subject, the feudal lords cannot make him a friend—I do not know the others."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven cannot enlist him as a subject, the lords cannot claim him as a friend. As for the rest—I would not know how to rank them."

sentences.zh: 〈《禮記》曰：「儒有上不臣天子，下不事諸侯。」〉

translations.literal: (The Record of Rites says: "The scholar at the top does not serve the Son of Heaven as subject; at the bottom he does not serve the feudal lords.")
translations.idiomatic: (The Liji puts it: the true scholar neither becomes the emperor's minister nor bends to a feudal lord.)

sentences.zh: 後遭母憂，有至孝稱。

translations.literal: Later, when he suffered his mother's death, he had a reputation for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he mourned with such devotion that his filial piety became proverbial.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承書曰：「遭母憂，歐血發病，歷年乃瘳。」〉

translations.literal: (Xie Cheng's Book says: "When he suffered his mother's death, he vomited blood and fell ill; only after a full year did he recover.")
translations.idiomatic: (Xie Cheng records that grief brought him to coughing blood and protracted illness before he recovered.)

sentences.zh: 林宗雖善人倫，而不爲危言覈論，

translations.literal: Although Linzong was skilled in judging human relations, he did not utter perilous words or harsh, searching judgments,
translations.idiomatic: Linzong read men shrewdly, yet he avoided incendiary language and cutting verdicts—

sentences.zh: 〈《禮記》曰：「擬人必於其倫。

translations.literal: (The Record of Rites says: "When comparing persons, one must do so in their proper category.
translations.idiomatic: (The Liji: "Judge a man only against his kind."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注曰：「倫猶類也。

translations.literal: "Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "lun means category.
translations.idiomatic: "Zheng Xuan glosses lun as "kind" or "class."

sentences.zh: 」論語孔子曰：「邦有道，危言危行。

translations.literal: "The Analects records Confucius: "When the state has the Way, one's words are bold and one's conduct is bold.
translations.idiomatic: "The Analects quotes Confucius: "When the state follows the Way, speak and act with bold integrity;

sentences.zh: 邦無道，危行言孫。

translations.literal: When the state lacks the Way, one's conduct is bold but one's words are deferential.
translations.idiomatic: when it does not, keep your conduct upright but humble your words."

sentences.zh: 」覈猶實也。〉

translations.literal: "he here means searching out the facts.)
translations.idiomatic: "Here he means "searching" or "probing to the truth.")

sentences.zh: 故宦官擅政而不能傷也。

translations.literal: Therefore, although the eunuchs monopolized government, they could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: So even when the eunuchs held the reins, they could not touch him.

sentences.zh: 及黨事起，知名之士多被其害，唯林宗及汝南袁閎得免焉。

translations.literal: When the faction case arose, many celebrated scholars suffered harm; only Linzong and Yuan Hong of Runan escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the proscription struck, most eminent scholars were ruined—Linzong and Yuan Hong of Runan alone were spared.

sentences.zh: 遂閉門敎授，弟子以千數。

translations.literal: Thereupon he closed his gate and taught; his disciples numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his doors to teach, and students flocked to him by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 明年春，卒于家，時年四十二。

translations.literal: The next spring he died at home, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he died at home at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 四方之士千餘人，皆來會葬。

translations.literal: More than a thousand scholars from the four quarters all came to join the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand men of learning traveled from every quarter to attend his burial.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承書曰：「泰以建寧二年正月卒，自弘農函谷關以西，河內湯陰以北，二千里負笈荷擔彌路，柴車葦裝塞塗，蓋有萬數來赴。」〉

translations.literal: (Xie Cheng's Book says: "Tai died in the first month of the second year of the Jianning era; from west of the Hongnong Hangu Pass to north of Tangyin in Henei, for two thousand li book-bearers and shoulder-pole carriers filled the roads; carts of brushwood and reed matting blocked the way—perhaps ten thousand came.")
translations.idiomatic: (Xie Cheng writes that when Guo Tai died in the first month of Jianning 2, mourners packed the roads for two thousand li—from west of Hangu in Hongnong to north of Tangyin in Henei—students with satchels, reed-wrapped carts, perhaps ten thousand strong.)

sentences.zh: 同志者乃共刻石立碑，蔡邕爲其文，旣而謂涿郡盧植曰：「吾爲碑銘多矣，皆有慙德，唯郭有道無愧色耳。」

translations.literal: Those of like mind then together carved stone and erected a stele; Cai Yong composed its text. Afterwards he said to Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: "I have written many stele inscriptions, and in all I have felt shame for my virtue—only for Guo Youdao do I feel no shame."
translations.idiomatic: His admirers raised a stone stele with an inscription by Cai Yong, who later told Lu Zhi of Zhuojun: "I have composed countless epitaphs, and most leave me uneasy about my own character—only Guo Youdao's leaves me untroubled."

sentences.zh: 其獎拔士人，皆如所鑒。

translations.literal: In every case his promotion of scholars matched what he had discerned.
translations.idiomatic: Every man he singled out for praise turned out just as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承書曰：「泰之所名，人品乃定，先言後驗，衆皆服之。

translations.literal: (Xie Cheng's Book says: "Whomever Tai named, that man's character was thereby fixed; he spoke first and it was verified afterward—all submitted to him.")
translations.idiomatic: (Xie Cheng: once Guo Tai pronounced on a man, opinion settled; prediction preceded proof, and everyone deferred to his judgment.)

sentences.zh: 故適陳留則友符偉明，遊太學則師仇季智，之陳國則親魏德公，入汝南則交黃叔度。

translations.literal: Therefore when he went to Chenliu he befriended Fu Weiming; when he roamed the Imperial Academy he took Qiu Jizhi as teacher; when he went to the Chen state he drew close to Wei Degong; when he entered Runan he associated with Huang Shudu.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenliu he befriended Fu Rong; at the Imperial Academy he studied under Qiu Jizhi; in Chen he grew close to Wei Lang; in Runan he joined Huang Xian.

sentences.zh: 初，太始至南州，過袁奉高，不宿而去；

translations.literal: At first, when Tai first arrived in the southern provinces, he passed Yuan Fenggao and did not stay the night but departed;
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Tai first came south, he called on Yuan Hong but stayed no night;

sentences.zh: 從叔度，累日不去。

translations.literal: with Shudu, many days he did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: with Huang Xian he lingered for days on end.

sentences.zh: 或以問太。

translations.literal: Someone thereupon questioned Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him why.

sentences.zh: 太曰：『奉高之器，譬之氿濫，雖清而易挹。

translations.literal: Tai said: "Fenggao's capacity is like a spring in a gully—though clear, it is easy to draw from.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai said: "Yuan Hong is like a clear spring in a hollow—bright enough, and easy to dip from.

sentences.zh: 叔度之器，汪汪若千頃之陂，澄之不清，擾之不濁，不可量也。

translations.literal: Shudu's capacity is vast as a thousand-qing pond—stir it and it will not clear, roil it and it will not grow turbid; it cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xian is like a thousand acres of still water: clarify it and it does not clear, churn it and it stays pure—too deep to measure.

sentences.zh: 』已而果然，太以是名聞天下。」〉

translations.literal: 』Afterward it proved so, and Tai by this was renowned throughout the world.")
translations.idiomatic: 』Events proved him right, and that judgment made Guo Tai's name known across the realm.")

sentences.zh: 後之好事，或附益增張，故多華辭不經，又類卜相之書。

translations.literal: Later enthusiasts sometimes appended and exaggerated, so there is much ornate language that is not canonical, and it also resembles divination and physiognomy texts.
translations.idiomatic: Later admirers embroidered the record with flourishes and tall tales, so much of what circulates is overwrought, unhistorical stuff that reads like fortune-telling manuals.

sentences.zh: 今錄其章章效於事者，著之篇末。

translations.literal: Now I record those that are manifestly verified in fact, appending them at the end of the chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Here I include only episodes that plainly hold up, set at the end of this chapter.

sentences.zh: 〈章章猶昭昭也。〉

translations.literal: (Zhangzhang is the same as zhaozhao—clearly evident.)
translations.idiomatic: (The reduplication zhangzhang means clearly or plainly.)

sentences.zh: 左原者，陳留人也。

translations.literal: Zuo Yuan was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Yuan came from Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 爲郡學生，犯法見斥。

translations.literal: He was a student of the commandery school; he violated the law and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A student in the commandery academy, he broke the rules and was expelled.

sentences.zh: 林宗甞遇諸路，爲設酒肴以慰之。

translations.literal: Linzong once met him on the road and for him set out wine and dishes to console him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai met him on the road once and laid out food and wine to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「昔顏涿聚梁甫之巨盜，段干木晉國之大駔，卒爲齊之忠臣，魏之名賢。

translations.literal: He said to him: "In former times Yan Zhuoju was a great bandit of Liangfu, Duan Ganmu a great broker of Jin; in the end they became a loyal minister of Qi and a celebrated worthy of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He told him: "Yan Zhuoju was a notorious brigand on Mount Liangfu; Duan Ganmu was Jin's leading broker—yet one became a loyal minister of Qi, the other a paragon in Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈《呂氏春秋》曰：「顏涿聚，梁父大盜也，學於孔子。

translations.literal: (The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Yan Zhuoju was a great bandit of Liangfu who studied with Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: (The Lüshi Chunqiu calls Yan Zhuoju a Liangfu outlaw who became Confucius's pupil.

sentences.zh: 」《左傳》曰：「晉伐齊，戰于黎丘，齊師敗績，親禽顏庚。

translations.literal: "The Zuo Zhuan says: "Jin attacked Qi and fought at Liqiu; the Qi army was routed, and [the Jin commander] personally captured Yan Geng.
translations.idiomatic: "The Zuo Zhuan records Jin's campaign against Qi at Liqiu—a rout, with Yan Geng taken alive.

sentences.zh: 」杜預注曰：「黎丘，隰也。

translations.literal: "Du Yu's commentary says: "Liqiu is Xi.
translations.idiomatic: "Du Yu identifies Liqiu with Xi.

sentences.zh: 顏庚，齊大夫顏涿聚也。

translations.literal: Yan Geng was the Qi grandee Yan Zhuoju.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Geng is Qi minister Yan Zhuoju.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「晉荀瑤伐鄭，鄭駟弘請救於齊。

translations.literal: "It also says: "Jin's Xun Yao attacked Zheng; Zheng's Si Hong requested aid from Qi.
translations.idiomatic: "Elsewhere: when Xun Yao of Jin attacked Zheng, Si Hong of Zheng begged Qi for help.

sentences.zh: 齊師將興，陳成子屬孤子，三日朝，設乘車兩馬，繫五邑焉。

translations.literal: When the Qi army was about to march, Chen Chengzi assigned orphans; for three days they held court, setting out two-horse chariots and attaching five settlements.
translations.idiomatic: As Qi mobilized, Chen Chengzi mustered the war orphans: three days of court, chariots and pairs of horses, five towns pledged to the cause.

sentences.zh: 召顏涿聚之子晉，曰：『隰之役，而父死焉，以國之多難，未汝恤也。

translations.literal: He summoned Yan Zhuoju's son Jin, saying: 『In the Xi campaign your father died there; because the state had many difficulties, we did not show you condolence.
translations.idiomatic: He called in Yan Jin, son of Yan Zhuoju: 『Your father fell at Xi; the realm was in such turmoil we never properly honored his sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今君命汝以是邑也，服車而朝，無廢前勞。

translations.literal: Now the lord commands you with regard to this settlement—attend court in your chariot; do not neglect your predecessor's labor.
translations.idiomatic: Now your lord invests you with this town—ride to court and do not dishonor your father's service.

sentences.zh: 』」《呂氏春秋》曰：「段干木，晉國之駔。

translations.literal: 』"The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Duan Ganmu was a broker of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: 』"The Lüshi Chunqiu adds: Duan Ganmu was Jin's market broker.

sentences.zh: 」《說文》曰：「駔，會也。

translations.literal: "The Shuowen says: "zang means broker.
translations.idiomatic: "The Shuowen defines zang as "agent" or "go-between."

sentences.zh: 謂合兩家之賣買，如今之度巿也。

translations.literal: It means joining the selling and buying of two parties, like today's market brokers.
translations.idiomatic: It denotes the middleman who brings buyer and seller together, as in a licensed market today.

sentences.zh: 」《新序》曰「魏文侯過段干木之閭而軾之，遂致祿百萬，而時往問之。

translations.literal: "The Xin Xu says "Marquis Wen of Wei, passing Duan Ganmu's lane, leaned on his chariot rail; thereupon he sent him a salary of a million and from time to time went to inquire of him.
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Xiang's Xin Xu tells how Marquis Wen of Wei bowed from his chariot at Duan Ganmu's lane, granted him a vast stipend, and called on him often.

sentences.zh: 國人皆喜，相與誦之曰：『吾君好正，段干木之敬；

translations.literal: The people of the state all rejoiced and together recited: 『Our lord loves rectitude—Duan Ganmu's reverence;
translations.idiomatic: The capital sang: 『Our lord loves uprightness—see how he honors Duan Ganmu;

sentences.zh: 吾君好忠，段干木之隆。

translations.literal: our lord loves loyalty—Duan Ganmu's eminence.
translations.idiomatic: our lord loves loyalty—see how he exalts Duan Ganmu.

sentences.zh: 』秦欲攻魏，司馬唐諫曰：『段干木賢者也，而魏禮之，天下莫不聞，無乃不可加兵乎？

translations.literal: 』Qin wished to attack Wei; Sima Tang remonstrated, saying: 『Duan Ganmu is a worthy man, and Wei treats him with ceremony—the whole world has heard of it—is it perhaps not fitting to refrain from applying arms?
translations.idiomatic: 』When Qin planned to strike Wei, Sima Tang objected: "Everyone knows Wei honors the worthy Duan Ganmu—surely this is no time to march."

sentences.zh: 』秦君以爲然」也。

translations.idiomatic: (Gloss: zang, reading zi-lang.)

translations.literal: Qu Boyu and Yan Hui still could not be without fault—how much more the rest?
translations.idiomatic: Even Qu Boyu and Yan Hui slipped sometimes—what mortal does not?

sentences.zh: 〈《論語》曰：「蘧伯玉使人於孔子，問之曰：『夫子何爲？

translations.literal: (The Analects says: "Qu Boyu sent someone to Confucius, who asked him: 『What is the Master doing?
translations.idiomatic: (The Analects: Qu Boyu's messenger asks Confucius's disciple, 『What has the Master been up to?

sentences.zh: 』對曰：『夫子欲寡其過而未能也。

translations.literal: 』He replied: 『The Master wishes to lessen his faults but has not yet been able.
translations.idiomatic: 』The answer: 『He is trying to have fewer faults—and still cannot manage it."

sentences.zh: 』」又曰：「顏回好學，不貳過。」〉

translations.idiomatic: 』"And Yan Hui "never made the same mistake twice.")

sentences.zh: 慎勿恚恨，責躬而已。

translations.literal: Be careful not to harbor resentment; blame only yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Do not nurse bitterness—look to your own conduct.

sentences.zh: 」原納其言而去。

translations.literal: "Yuan accepted his words and departed.
translations.idiomatic: "Zuo Yuan took the advice and left.

sentences.zh: 或有譏林宗不絕惡人者。

translations.literal: Some criticized Linzong for not cutting off evil men.
translations.idiomatic: Some faulted Guo Tai for not shunning wrongdoers outright.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「人而不仁，疾之以甚，亂也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "For a person who lacks humaneness, to hate him excessively is to bring disorder."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "To heap scorn on the unworthy only deepens the trouble—that is what Confucius meant."

sentences.zh: 〈《論語》孔子之言也。

translations.literal: (These are the words of Confucius in the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: (A line from Confucius in the Analects.)

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：「不仁之人，當以風化之。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary states: "As for a person who lacks humaneness, he should be transformed by moral influence.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses the passage: the unworthy ought to be reformed by example and teaching, not crushed.

sentences.zh: 若疾之以甚，是益使爲亂也。」〉

translations.literal: If you hate him excessively, this only makes him turn all the more to disorder.")
translations.idiomatic: To pursue him with bitter hatred only drives him further into rebellion.")

sentences.zh: 原後忽更懷忿，結客欲報諸生。

translations.literal: Later Yuan suddenly harbored resentment again; he gathered retainers intending to take revenge on the students.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Yuan later nursed a fresh grudge and recruited bravos to settle scores with the school.

sentences.zh: 其日林宗在學，原愧負前言，因遂罷去。

translations.literal: That day Linzong was at the school; Yuan felt ashamed of having betrayed his earlier words, and therefore desisted and left.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai happened to be at the academy that day; shamed by his own earlier pledge, Zuo Yuan abandoned the plot.

sentences.zh: 後事露，衆人咸謝服焉。

translations.literal: Later when the affair was exposed, everyone thanked him and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, the community acknowledged Guo Tai's foresight with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 茅容字季偉，陳留人也。

translations.literal: Mao Rong, style name Jiwei, was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Rong, courtesy name Jiwei, came from Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，耕於野，時與等輩避雨樹下，衆皆夷踞相對，

translations.literal: Past forty, he was ploughing in the fields; once he took shelter from rain under a tree with his peers—all sat with legs stretched flat, facing one another,
translations.idiomatic: In his forties he still farmed; caught in a shower with companions under a tree, the rest lounged in casual poses—

sentences.zh: 〈夷，平也。

translations.literal: (yi means flat.
translations.idiomatic: (Here yi means flat or level—

translations.idiomatic: the Shuowen glosses ju as squatting.)

sentences.zh: 容獨危坐愈恭。

translations.literal: Rong alone sat upright with knees together, all the more respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Rong alone sat bolt upright, the picture of respect.

sentences.zh: 林宗行見之而竒其異，遂與共言，因請寓宿。

translations.literal: Linzong, passing, saw this and thought it strange; he conversed with him and asked to lodge overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai noticed, struck by the contrast, spoke with him and asked to stay the night.

sentences.zh: 旦日，容殺雞爲饌，林宗謂爲己設，旣而以供其母，自以草蔬與客同飯。

translations.literal: Next morning Rong killed a chicken for a meal; Linzong thought it was prepared for himself, but Rong then served it to his mother, while he himself took coarse greens and ate with his guest.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Mao slaughtered a fowl; Guo Tai assumed it was for him, but the meat went to Mao's mother while host and guest shared plain vegetables.

sentences.zh: 〈草，麤也。〉

translations.literal: (Cao means coarse.)
translations.idiomatic: (Here cao denotes coarse forage.)

sentences.zh: 林宗起拜之曰：「卿賢乎哉！

translations.literal: Linzong rose and bowed to him, saying: "You are a worthy man indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai rose and bowed: "You are a true gentleman!

sentences.zh: 」因勸令學，卒以成德。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he urged him to study, and in the end he achieved moral completion.
translations.idiomatic: "He urged him into scholarship, and Mao Rong matured into a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 孟敏字叔達，鉅鹿楊氏人也。

translations.literal: Meng Min, style name Shuda, was a man of Yangshi in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Min, courtesy name Shuda, was a native of Yangshi in Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《十三州志》曰：楊氏縣在今魏郡北也。〉

translations.literal: (The Records of the Thirteen Provinces says: Yangshi county lies north of present-day Wei commandery.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Thirteen Provinces gazetteer places Yangshi north of Wei commandery as it is today.)

sentences.zh: 客居太原。

translations.literal: He resided as a guest in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was living in Taiyuan as a sojourner.

sentences.zh: 荷甑墯地，不顧而去。

translations.literal: Carrying a steamer on his back, he dropped it to the ground and walked off without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: His steamer slipped from his shoulder; he walked on without a backward glance.

sentences.zh: 林宗見而問其意。

translations.literal: Linzong saw this and asked his intention.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai asked why he had not stopped.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「甑以破矣，視之何益？

translations.literal: He replied: "The steamer is already broken—what use to look at it?
translations.idiomatic: Meng Min said: "The pot is shattered. Staring at the shards helps nothing.

sentences.zh: 」林宗以此異之，因勸令遊學。

translations.literal: "Linzong considered this extraordinary and urged him to travel and study.
translations.idiomatic: "Guo Tai marked him as exceptional and urged him to study abroad.

sentences.zh: 十年知名，三公俱辟，並不屈云。

translations.literal: After ten years he was well known; the Three Ducal Offices all summoned him, and he consistently refused.
translations.idiomatic: Within a decade his name was known; all three highest offices called him, and he declined every time.

sentences.zh: 庾乘字世遊，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Cheng, style name Shiyou, was a man of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cheng, courtesy name Shiyou, hailed from Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 少給事縣廷爲門士。

translations.literal: In youth he served in the county yamen as a gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he worked the county gate as a clerk-guard.

sentences.zh: 〈士即門卒。〉

translations.literal: (shi here means gate sentry.)
translations.idiomatic: (Here shi denotes the gate watchman.)

sentences.zh: 林宗見而拔之，勸遊學官，遂爲諸生傭。

translations.literal: Linzong saw him and singled him out, urging him to study at the academy; thereupon he became a hired hand for the students.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai noticed him, urged him into the Imperial Academy, and he paid his way by working for fellow students.

sentences.zh: 後能講論，自以卑第，每處下坐，諸生博士皆就讎問，由是學中以下坐爲貴。

translations.literal: Later he was able to lecture and discuss; considering himself of low rank, he always took the lowest seat—students and erudites all came to him with questions, and on this account in the school the lowest seat was esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: He grew able to hold his own in debate; out of modesty he always took the back bench, yet scholars and doctors flocked to him for answers—until the academy made a virtue of sitting low.

sentences.zh: 後徵辟並不起，號曰「徵君」。

translations.literal: Later summons and recommendations alike he did not accept; he was styled "Gentleman Summoned".
translations.idiomatic: He ignored every summons and came to be known as the "recluse who refused appointment."

sentences.zh: 宋果字仲乙，

translations.literal: Song Guo, style name Zhongyi,
translations.idiomatic: Song Guo, courtesy name Zhongyi (or Zhongwen—see note),

sentences.zh: 〈謝承書「乙」作「文」。〉

translations.literal: (In Xie Cheng's Book "yi" is written "wen".)
translations.idiomatic: (Xie Cheng's text reads the second character as wen instead of yi.)

sentences.zh: 扶風人也。

translations.literal: He was a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was from Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 性輕悍，憙與人報讎，爲郡縣所疾。

translations.literal: By nature he was rash and fierce, fond of avenging grudges for others, and was detested by the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He was hot-tempered and lived to settle other men's feuds—local officials loathed him.

sentences.zh: 林宗乃訓之義方，懼以禍敗。

translations.literal: Linzong then instructed him in right principle, frightening him with the prospect of disaster and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai taught him the right way and warned him where violence would end.

sentences.zh: 果感悔，叩頭謝負，遂改節自勑。

translations.literal: Guo was moved to repentance; he knocked his head in apology for his faults, and thereupon changed his conduct and disciplined himself.
translations.idiomatic: Song Guo repented, kowtowed in acknowledgment of his wrongs, and reformed his life.

sentences.zh: 後以烈氣聞，辟公府，侍御史、并州刺史，所在能化。

translations.literal: Later he became known for stern integrity; he was summoned to the Ducal Offices, served as attendant censor and Inspector of Bing province, and wherever he went was able to transform [the people].
translations.idiomatic: He won a reputation for stern integrity, entered the central administration, rose to attendant censor and governor of Bing, and left a record of moral sway wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 賈淑字子厚，林宗鄉人也。

translations.literal: Jia Shu, style name Zihou, was a fellow townsman of Linzong.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Shu, courtesy name Zihou, came from Guo Tai's home district.

sentences.zh: 雖世有冠冕，而性險害，邑里患之。

translations.literal: Although his family had held high caps [office], his nature was treacherous and harmful, and the village dreaded him.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had worn official caps, but he was vicious, and the neighborhood lived in fear of him.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承書曰：「淑爲舅宋瑗報讎於縣中，爲吏所捕，繫獄當死。

translations.literal: (Xie Cheng's Book says: "Shu avenged his uncle Song Yuan in the county seat; he was seized by the clerks, imprisoned, and faced execution.
translations.idiomatic: (Xie Cheng: Jia Shu had avenged his uncle Song Yuan in town, been arrested, and faced the death cell—

sentences.zh: 泰與語，淑懇惻流涕。

translations.literal: Tai spoke with him; Shu was earnest and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai spoke with him until Jia Shu wept with remorse.

sentences.zh: 泰詣縣令應操，陳其報怨蹈義之士。

translations.literal: Tai went to Magistrate Ying Cao and set forth that he was a man who had avenged a grievance in the cause of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai went to Magistrate Ying Cao and argued that Jia had acted from righteous duty in a blood feud.

sentences.zh: 被赦，縣不宥之，郡上言，乃得原。」〉

translations.literal: An amnesty was issued, but the county would not pardon him; the commandery memorialized upward, and only then was he forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Though an amnesty had passed, the county would not release him until the commandery appealed—then he was spared.

sentences.zh: 林宗遭母憂，淑來修弔，旣而鉅鹿孫威直亦至。

translations.literal: When Linzong suffered his mother's death, Shu came to pay condolence; presently Sun Weizhi of Julu also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Tai mourned his mother, Jia Shu came to offer condolences—soon joined by Sun Weizhi from Julu.

sentences.zh: 威直以林宗賢而受惡人弔，心怪之，不進而去。

translations.literal: Weizhi, because Linzong was worthy yet received condolence from a wicked man, thought it strange in his heart; he did not enter but departed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun took offense that so worthy a man would admit a known villain; he turned on his heel without entering.

sentences.zh: 林宗追而謝之曰：「賈子厚誠實凶德，然洗心向善。

translations.literal: Linzong pursued him and apologized, saying: "Jia Zihou is indeed of vicious virtue, yet he has washed his heart and turned toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai overtook him and explained: "Jia Shu has an ugly past, but he is trying to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 仲尼不逆互鄉，故吾許其進也。」

translations.literal: Confucius did not reject Huxiang—therefore I permit his advance."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius did not turn away the village of Hu—so I accept his coming."

sentences.zh: 〈互鄉，鄉名。

translations.idiomatic: (Huxiang was a place-name—

sentences.zh: 「互鄉難與言，童子見，門人惑。

translations.literal: "Huxiang is hard to talk with; a boy was received to see [Confucius], and the disciples were perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: the Analects calls it hard to deal with; when Confucius saw a boy from there, his disciples were puzzled.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『人潔己以進，與其進，不保其往。』」〉

translations.literal: Confucius said: 『When someone purifies himself to advance, approve his advance—do not guarantee his past.』")
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: approve the man who comes having cleansed himself—do not hold his old sins against him.』")

sentences.zh: 淑聞之，改過自厲，終成善士。

translations.literal: When Shu heard this, he corrected his faults and disciplined himself, and in the end became a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Shu took the lesson to heart, reformed, and became a respected man.

sentences.zh: 鄉里有憂患者，淑輒傾身營救，爲州閭所稱。

translations.literal: When the village had troubles and worries, Shu always threw himself into rescue, and was praised by the district.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever neighbors faced disaster, Jia Shu threw himself into relief work and won praise across the canton.

sentences.zh: 史叔賔

translations.literal: Shi Shubin
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shubin

sentences.zh: 史叔賔者，陳留人也。

translations.literal: Shi Shubin was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shubin came from Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 少有盛名。

translations.literal: In youth he had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he enjoyed outsized fame.

sentences.zh: 林宗見而告人曰：「牆高基下，雖得必失。

translations.literal: Linzong saw him and told others: "The wall is high but the foundation is low—though you may gain, you will surely lose.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai remarked to others: "Tall walls on shallow footings—whatever he wins now, he will lose.

sentences.zh: 」後果以論議阿枉敗名云。

translations.literal: "Later indeed, through discourse that bent and twisted, he ruined his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: "He was later disgraced when his opinions proved crooked and self-serving.

sentences.zh: 黃允字子艾，濟陰人也。

translations.literal: Huang Yun, style name Ziai, was a man of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yun, courtesy name Ziai, was from Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 以儁才知名。

translations.literal: He was known for outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: His brilliance made his name.

sentences.zh: 林宗見而謂曰：「卿有絕人之才，足成偉器。

translations.literal: Linzong saw him and said: "You have talent that surpasses others, enough to become a great vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai told him: "You have gifts few can match—you could be a man of consequence.

sentences.zh: 然恐守道不篤，將失之矣。

translations.literal: Yet I fear you do not hold fast to the Way with constancy—you are about to lose it.
translations.idiomatic: But unless you hold the moral course firmly, you will throw it all away.

sentences.zh: 」後司徒袁隗欲爲從女求姻，見允而歎曰：「得壻如是足矣。

translations.literal: "Later Minister of Education Yuan Kui wished to seek a marriage alliance for his niece; seeing Yun he sighed: "To obtain a son-in-law like this would be enough.
translations.idiomatic: "Minister Yuan Kui later sought a husband for his niece; one look at Huang Yun drew a sigh: "A son-in-law like him would satisfy any family.

sentences.zh: 」允聞而黜遣其妻夏侯氏。

translations.literal: "When Yun heard this, he dismissed and sent away his wife, Lady Xiahou.
translations.idiomatic: "Huang Yun divorced his wife of the Xiahou clan to clear the way.

sentences.zh: 婦謂姑曰：「今當見弃，方與黃氏長辭，乞一會親屬，以展離訣之情。

translations.literal: The wife said to her mother-in-law: "Now that I am about to be cast off, I am about to take long leave of the Huang household; I beg one gathering of kin to express the feelings of parting.
translations.idiomatic: She told her mother-in-law: "Before the Huangs cast me out, let me face my kin once to say goodbye.

sentences.zh: 」於是大集賔客三百餘人，婦中坐，攘袂數允隱匿穢惡十五事，言畢，登車而去。

translations.literal: "Thereupon she greatly assembled more than three hundred guests; the wife sat in their midst, rolled up her sleeves, and enumerated fifteen hidden vile deeds of Yun; when she finished speaking, she mounted a carriage and departed.
translations.idiomatic: "She invited three hundred guests, took the seat of honor, pushed up her sleeves, and recited fifteen of Huang Yun's secret shames—then stepped into her carriage and left.

sentences.zh: 允以此廢於時。

translations.literal: Yun on account of this was cast aside in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yun was ruined in the eyes of his generation.

sentences.zh: 謝甄字子微，汝南召陵人也。

translations.literal: Xie Zhen, style name Ziwei, was a man of Shaoling in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhen (distinct from the historian Xie Cheng), courtesy name Ziwei, hailed from Shaoling in Runan.

sentences.zh: 與陳留邊讓並善談論，俱有盛名。

translations.literal: Together with Bian Rang of Chenliu he was skilled in discussion; both had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He and Bian Rang of Chenliu were famed debaters with glittering reputations.

sentences.zh: 每共候林宗，未甞不連日達夜。

translations.literal: Whenever together they waited upon Linzong, it was never not continuously from day into night.
translations.idiomatic: Their visits to Guo Tai routinely stretched from dawn past midnight.

sentences.zh: 林宗謂門人曰：「二子英才有餘，而並不入道，惜乎！

translations.literal: Linzong said to his disciples: "These two have surplus heroic talent, yet neither enters the Way—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai told students: "Both men brim with brilliance, yet neither will commit to the true path—what a waste!

sentences.zh: 」甄後不拘細行，爲時所毀。

translations.literal: "Later Zhen did not restrain himself in small conduct, and was slandered by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: "Xie Zhen later scorned small scruples and fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 讓以輕侮曹操，操殺之。

translations.literal: Rang treated Cao Cao with contempt; Cao killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Rang insulted Cao Cao and paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 王柔字叔優，弟澤，字季道，林宗同郡晉陽縣人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rou, style name Shuyou, and his younger brother Ze, style name Jidao, were men of Jinyang county in the same commandery as Linzong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rou (courtesy Shuyou) and his brother Wang Ze (courtesy Jidao) were from Jinyang—Guo Tai's home commandery.

sentences.zh: 兄弟緫角共候林宗，以訪才行所宜。

translations.literal: The brothers, with hair in tufts [as children], together waited upon Linzong to inquire what their talents and conduct suited.
translations.idiomatic: Still in their youth they called on Guo Tai to learn where their talents pointed.

sentences.zh: 林宗曰：「叔優當以仕進顯，季道當以經術通，然違方改務，亦不能至也。

translations.literal: Linzong said: "Shuyou should become eminent through office-seeking; Jidao should penetrate through classical learning—yet if they turn aside from these directions and change their pursuits, they will not reach it either.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai said: "Rou will rise through public service, Ze through scholarship—stray from those paths and neither will fulfill his promise.

sentences.zh: 」後果如所言，柔爲護匈奴中郎將，澤爲代郡太守。

translations.literal: "Later it was indeed as he said: Rou became Colonel of the Protectorate of the Xiongnu; Ze became Governor of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: "So it proved: Wang Rou commanded the Xiongnu protectorate; Wang Ze governed Dai.

sentences.zh: 又識張孝仲芻牧之中，知范特祖郵置之役，

translations.literal: He also recognized Zhang Xiaozhong among herders of fodder, and knew Fan Tizu in the service of the post stations,
translations.idiomatic: He spotted Zhang Xiaozhong herding cattle and Fan Tizu working the post road—

sentences.zh: 〈《說文》曰：「郵，境上傳書舍也。

translations.literal: Young Lord Shao and Xu Weikang both came out of butchery and liquor-selling; Sima Ziwei was raised from the ranks; together with Guo Changxin, Wang Changwen, Han Wenbu, Li Zizheng, Cao Ziyuan of the same commandery, Zhou Kangzi of Dingxiang, Wang Jiran of Xihe, Qiu Jizhi of Yunzhong, Hao Lizhen, and others—sixty men in all—all became established in reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He picked Shao Gongzi and Xu Weikang from the butcher's stall, Sima Ziwei from the ranks, and alongside fifty-seven others—Guo Changxin, Wang Changwen, Han Wenbu, Li Zizheng, Cao Ziyuan, Zhou Kangzi, Wang Jiran, Qiu Jizhi, Hao Lizhen, and the rest from Taiyuan and beyond—each won a name.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承書曰：「太原郭長信、王長文、長文弟子師、韓文布、李子政、曹子元、定襄周康子、西河王季然、雲中丘季智名靈舉。

translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Zhuangzi observed that human hearts are trickier than mountain passes—outward motion is easy to read, but what lies hidden resists scrutiny.

translations.literal: (Gui means to oppose or diverge.)
translations.idiomatic: (Gui: to diverge or conflict.)

translations.literal: The mirror of discerning wisdom is what even the Emperor finds difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Even the sage-kings struggled to judge men aright.

translations.idiomatic: as the Shang shu says: knowing men is the hardest test even for a sovereign.")

sentences.zh: 而林宗雅俗無所失，將其明性特有主乎？

translations.literal: Yet Linzong had no failures with refined and vulgar alike—was it that his enlightened nature had a special master?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guo Tai read high and low without error—did he possess an almost uncanny clarity?

sentences.zh: 然而遜言危行，終亨時晦，

translations.literal: Yet deferential in speech, perilous in conduct, in the end he penetrated the times and veiled his brightness,
translations.idiomatic: He spoke softly, acted cautiously, and thrived by hiding his light through dark times—

sentences.zh: 〈亨，通也。〉

translations.literal: (Heng means to penetrate or succeed.)
translations.idiomatic: (Heng: to succeed or prevail.)

sentences.zh: 恂恂善導，使士慕成名，雖墨、孟之徒，不能絕也。

translations.literal: Courteous and good at guiding, causing scholars to yearn to establish a name—even followers of Mo and Meng could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Guiding disciples with gentle persistence until they hungered for renown—even Mozi and Mencius could scarcely have surpassed that gift.

sentences.zh: 〈墨翟、孟軻也。

translations.idiomatic: (The text means Mozi and Mencius—

translations.idiomatic: jue: to surpass.)

sentences.zh: 符融字偉明，陳留浚儀人也。

translations.literal: Fu Rong, style name Weiming, was a man of Junyi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong, courtesy name Weiming, came from Junyi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 少爲都官吏，恥之，委去。

translations.literal: In youth he was a clerk for the commandery capital; ashamed of it, he abandoned the post.
translations.idiomatic: His first job was a low clerkship in the commandery seat—he quit out of shame.

sentences.zh: 〈《續漢志》曰：「都官從事，主察舉百官犯法者。

translations.literal: (The Treatise on the Continued Han says: "The metropolitan investigator is charged with investigating and reporting officials who violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: (According to the Xu Han zhi, the capital "metropolitan investigator" policed wrongdoing among the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 」融恥爲其吏而去。〉

translations.literal: "Rong was ashamed to serve as such a clerk and left.)
translations.idiomatic: "Fu Rong resigned rather than hold that post.)

sentences.zh: 後遊太學，師事少府李膺。

translations.literal: Later he studied at the Imperial Academy, serving Minister of the Household Li Ying as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered the Imperial Academy and took Li Ying, the Minister of the Household, as his master.

sentences.zh: 膺風性高簡，每見融，輒絕它賔客，聽其言論。

translations.literal: Ying's manner and nature were lofty and reserved; whenever he saw Rong, he would cut off all other guests and listen to his discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying was austere and aloof; whenever Fu Rong called, he sent other visitors away to hear him speak.

sentences.zh: 融幅巾奮褎，談辭如雲，

translations.literal: Rong in a wrapped headcloth and rolling up his sleeves, his words of discussion like clouds,
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong wore a scholar's headwrap, gestured with sweeping sleeves, and let argument pour forth like a cloudburst—

sentences.zh: 〈幅巾者，以一幅爲之也。

translations.literal: (A wrapped headcloth is made from a single breadth of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: (The "wrapped headcloth" is a single width of fabric—

sentences.zh: 褎，古袖字。

translations.literal: xiu is the ancient graph for sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: xiu is the old form of "sleeve."

sentences.zh: 如雲者，奔踊而出也。〉

translations.literal: "Like clouds" means they surge forth in a rush.)
translations.idiomatic: "Like clouds" describes eloquence that surges out.)

sentences.zh: 膺每捧手歎息。

translations.literal: Ying each time clasped his hands and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying would clasp his hands and sigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 郭林宗始入京師，時人莫識，融一見嗟服，因以介於李膺，由是知名。

translations.literal: When Guo Linzong first entered the capital, people of the time did not know him; Rong at one sight sighed in admiration, and on that account introduced him to Li Ying—thereby he became known.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Tai first reached the capital, nobody knew him; Fu Rong recognized his quality at once and introduced him to Li Ying—that was how Guo Tai's name spread.

sentences.zh: 〈古人相見，必因紹介。

translations.literal: (In antiquity when people met, they always went through introduction.
translations.idiomatic: (Ancient etiquette required an introduction—

sentences.zh: 介，因也，言因此人以相接見也。

translations.literal: jie means "by means of"—that is, by means of this person to connect and meet.
translations.idiomatic: "Introduce" here means to bring two parties together through a third.

sentences.zh: 謝承書曰：「融見林宗，便與之交。

translations.literal: Xie Cheng's Book says: "When Rong saw Linzong, he immediately befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng records that Fu Rong befriended Guo Tai on sight—

sentences.zh: 又紹介於膺，以爲海之明珠，未燿其光，鳥之鳳皇，羽儀未翔。

translations.literal: He also introduced him to Ying, saying he was like a bright pearl of the sea whose luster had not yet shone, a phoenix among birds whose pinions had not yet soared.
translations.idiomatic: then presented him to Li Ying as a pearl still hidden in the sea, a phoenix whose wings had not yet spread.

sentences.zh: 膺與林宗相見，待以師友之禮，遂振名天下，融之致也。」〉

translations.literal: When Ying and Linzong met, he treated him with the rites due to teacher and friend; thereupon his fame shook the world—this was Rong's doing.")
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying received Guo Tai as equal and mentor, and Guo's reputation shook the realm—that was Fu Rong's doing.")

sentences.zh: 時漢中晉文經、梁國黃子艾，並恃其才智，炫曜上京，卧託養疾，無所通接。

translations.literal: At that time Jin Wenjing of Hanzhong and Huang Ziai of Liang state, both relying on their talent and wisdom, displayed themselves in the upper capital, feigning illness and lying abed, receiving no one.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wenjing of Hanzhong and Huang Ziai of Liang had been trading on clever reputations in Luoyang, pretending to be ill and refusing visitors.

sentences.zh: 洛中士大夫好事者，承其聲名，坐門問疾，猶不得見。

translations.literal: Among Luoyang gentry and scholars who loved such things, accepting their reputation, they sat at the gate and inquired after their illness—yet still could not obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Fashionable officials camped on their doorsteps to ask after their health and still could not get in.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承書曰：「文經、子艾，曜名遠近，聲價已定，徵辟不就，療病京師，不通賔客。

translations.literal: (Xie Cheng's Book says: "Wenjing and Ziai shone their names far and near; their price in reputation was already fixed; they did not respond to summons; they treated illness in the capital and did not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: (Xie Cheng: the pair had fixed their market value, ignored appointments, "convalesced" in the capital, and barred callers—

sentences.zh: 公卿將相大夫遣門生旦暮問疾，郎吏公府掾屬雜坐其門，不得見也。」〉

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, generals, and grandees sent disciples morning and evening to inquire after illness; gentlemen-attendants and clerks of the Ducal Offices sat in a jumble at their gate—yet could not see them.")
translations.idiomatic: while grandees sent pupils day and night and junior officials clogged the lane—still no audience.")

sentences.zh: 三公所辟召者，輒以詢訪之，隨所臧否，以爲與奪。

translations.literal: Whomever the Three Ducal Offices summoned, they would consult these two; according to their praise or blame, appointments were granted or withheld.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Ducal Offices deferred to the pair on every nomination—approval or veto followed their word.

sentences.zh: 融察其非真，乃到太學，并見李膺曰：「二子行業無聞，以豪桀自置，遂使公卿問疾，王臣坐門。

translations.literal: Rong perceived they were not genuine; he then went to the Imperial Academy and together saw Li Ying, saying: "These two have no known conduct or achievement; they set themselves up as heroes, with the result that dukes and ministers inquire after illness and royal ministers sit at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong saw through the fraud, went to the academy with Li Ying, and said: "These men have no record of merit; they pose as prodigies while ministers grovel at sickbeds.

sentences.zh: 融恐其小道破義，空譽違實，特宜察焉。

translations.literal: Rong fears their petty ways will destroy rectitude—empty reputation at odds with reality; they especially ought to be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: I fear petty imposture is corrupting public trust—empty fame needs exposing.

sentences.zh: 」膺然之。

translations.literal: "Ying assented.
translations.idiomatic: "Li Ying agreed.

sentences.zh: 二人自是名論漸衰，賔徒稍省，旬日之閒，慙歎逃去。

translations.literal: Thereafter the two men's reputations gradually declined, their followers slightly diminished; within ten days they shamefully sighed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Their stock fell, their retinues thinned; within days they slunk away in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 後果爲輕薄子，並以罪廢弃。

translations.literal: Later they indeed proved to be frivolous fellows; both were cast aside for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Both turned out to be worthless men, ruined by scandal.

sentences.zh: 融益以知名。

translations.literal: Rong thereby became all the more known.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong's own reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮請，舉孝廉，公府連辟，皆不應。

translations.literal: The province and commandery courteously invited him; he was recommended as filial and incorrupt; the Ducal Offices repeatedly summoned him—he did not respond to any.
translations.idiomatic: He turned down provincial honors, the filial-and-incorrupt nomination, and repeated calls from the capital.

sentences.zh: 太守馮岱有名稱，到官，請融相見。

translations.literal: Governor Feng Dai had a good reputation; when he arrived in office, he requested to meet Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Feng Dai, a respected official, asked to see him on taking office.

sentences.zh: 融一往，薦達郡士范冉、韓卓、孔伷等三人，

translations.literal: Rong went once and recommended and advanced three commandery scholars—Fan Ran, Han Zhuo, Kong Zhou, and others,
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong went once and put forward Fan Ran, Han Zhuo, and Kong Zhou—

translations.idiomatic: (Reading: same syllable as in "helmet.")

translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng identifies Feng Dai, courtesy Deshan—

sentences.zh: 性忼慨，有文武異才。

translations.literal: His nature is forthright and generous; he has unusual talent in both civil and military matters.
translations.idiomatic: a generous man of unusual civil and military gifts.

sentences.zh: 旣到官，融往相見，薦范冉爲功曹，韓卓爲主簿，孔伷爲上計吏。

translations.literal: When he had arrived in office, Rong went to meet him and recommended Fan Ran as merit assessor, Han Zhuo as chief clerk, and Kong Zhou as accounts envoy.

sentences.zh: 因辭病自絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he declined on grounds of illness and cut himself off.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong then pleaded illness and broke off contact.

translations.literal: When the faction case occurred, he also suffered proscription.
translations.idiomatic: The faction proscription caught him as well.

translations.literal: When his wife died, he was too poor for burial rites; fellow villagers wished to provide coffin and garments, but Rong would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife died he could not afford a funeral; neighbors offered a coffin and shroud, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 曰：「古之亡者，弃之中野。

translations.literal: He said: "In antiquity the dead were abandoned in the open wilds.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "The ancients left the dead in the open field.

sentences.zh: 〈易繫詞曰：「古之葬者，厚衣以薪，葬之中野。」〉

translations.literal: (The Appended Remarks to the Changes says: "In ancient burials, they thickly clothed [the corpse] with firewood and buried it in the open wilds.")
translations.idiomatic: (The Yijing Xici: early burials wrapped the dead in brush and laid them in the wild.)

translations.literal: Only wife and children may carry out one's intent—only bury in the earth on the spot—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Only family may carry out my wish—a simple earthen burial is enough."

translations.idiomatic: He offered his own ox-cart for the procession, and Fu Rong accepted.")

sentences.zh: 融同郡田盛，字仲嚮，與郭林宗同好，亦名知人，優遊不仕，並以壽終。

translations.literal: Tian Sheng of the same commandery as Rong, style name Zhongxiang, shared Guo Linzong's tastes, was also famed for knowing men, wandered at leisure and did not take office—both ended their lives in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Sheng of the same district—courtesy Zhongxiang—shared Guo Tai's interests and gift for reading men; both lived out their years without serving.

sentences.zh: 許劭字子將，汝南平輿人也。

translations.literal: Xu Shao, style name Zijiang, was a man of Pingyu in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao, courtesy name Zijiang, came from Pingyu in Runan.

sentences.zh: 〈輿音預。〉

translations.literal: (yu is pronounced yu.)
translations.idiomatic: (Gloss: Yu, fourth tone.)

sentences.zh: 少峻名節，好人倫，多所賞識。

translations.literal: In youth he was strict about reputation and integrity, fond of judging human relations, and made many appraisals.
translations.idiomatic: Young and strict in matters of integrity, he loved ranking character and passed judgment often.

sentences.zh: 若樊子昭、和陽士者，並顯名於世。

translations.literal: Such as Fan Zizhao and He Yangshi—both became illustrious names in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zizhao and He Yangshi were among those whose fame his verdicts helped establish.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》曰：「和洽字陽士，汝南西平人也。

translations.literal: (The Wei zhi says: "He Qia, style name Yangshi, was a man of Xiping in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: (The Records of Wei: He Qia, courtesy Yangshi, from Xiping in Runan—

sentences.zh: 初舉孝廉，大將軍辟，不就。

translations.literal: At first he was recommended as filial and incorrupt; the Grand General summoned him—he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: recommended as filial and incorrupt, he declined the generalissimo's summons—

sentences.zh: 魏國建，爲侍中。」〉

translations.literal: When the Wei state was established, he became palace attendant.")
translations.idiomatic: and when Wei was founded he became a palace attendant.")

translations.literal: Therefore when the world spoke of elevating scholars, all named Xu and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Hence everyone who spoke of talent-spotting paired "Xu and Guo."

sentences.zh: 初爲郡功曹，太守徐璆甚敬之。

translations.literal: At first he was merit assessor of the commandery; Governor Xu Qiu greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: He began as merit assessor under Governor Xu Qiu, who held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 〈璆音求，又巨秋反。〉

translations.literal: (qiu is pronounced qiu, also ju-qiu fanqie.)
translations.idiomatic: (Xu Qiu: reading qiu.)

sentences.zh: 府中聞子將爲吏，莫不改操飾行。

translations.literal: When the offices heard that Zijiang would serve as clerk, there was none who did not reform conduct and adorn behavior.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that Xu Shao would take office, every clerk in the yamen cleaned up his act.

sentences.zh: 同郡袁紹，公族豪俠，去濮陽令歸，車徒甚盛，將入郡界，乃謝遣賔客，曰：「吾輿服豈可使許子將見。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao of the same commandery, a noble clan stalwart, left the magistracy of Puyang and returned; his carriages and followers were very grand. About to enter the commandery border, he then dismissed his guests with thanks, saying: "How could I let my carriage and dress be seen by Xu Zijiang?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao, returning from Puyang in a grand train, dismissed his escort at the border: "I will not parade finery before Xu Shao.

sentences.zh: 」遂以單車歸家。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he returned home in a single cart.
translations.idiomatic: "He rode home alone in a plain cart.

sentences.zh: 劭甞到潁川，多長者之遊，唯不候陳寔。

translations.literal: Shao once went to Yingchuan and visited many elders—only he did not call on Chen Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Yingchuan, he paid his respects to every notable except Chen Shi.

sentences.zh: 又陳蕃喪妻還葬，鄉人畢至，而劭獨不往。

translations.literal: Moreover when Chen Fan lost his wife and returned her for burial, all the villagers arrived, but Shao alone did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Fan brought his wife home for burial, the whole district turned out—Xu Shao stayed away.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，劭曰：「太丘道廣，廣則難周；

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason; Shao said: "Taqiu's way is broad—when broad, it is hard to be thorough;
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said: "Chen Shi casts his net wide—too wide to cover everything;

sentences.zh: 仲舉性峻，峻則少通。

translations.literal: Zhongju's nature is severe—when severe, there is little accommodation.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan is rigid—rigidity leaves little room for nuance.

sentences.zh: 故不造也。

translations.literal: Therefore I do not visit.
translations.idiomatic: So I keep my distance from both.

sentences.zh: 」其多所裁量若此。

translations.literal: "His many judgments were like this.
translations.idiomatic: "Such was the edge of his judgments.

sentences.zh: 曹操微時，常卑辭厚禮，求爲己目。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao was obscure, he often used humble words and lavish gifts, seeking to have [Xu Shao] compose a "label" for him.
translations.idiomatic: In his obscure days Cao Cao flattered Xu Shao with gifts, begging for a character appraisal.

sentences.zh: 〈令品藻爲題目。〉

translations.literal: (This means to have him assess character and set a "title".)
translations.idiomatic: ("Label" means a summative verdict on character.)

sentences.zh: 劭鄙其人而不肯對，操乃伺隙脅劭，劭不得已，曰：「君清平之姦賊，亂世之英雄。

translations.literal: Shao despised the man and would not answer; Cao then watched for an opening and coerced Shao; Shao had no choice but to say: "You are a villain under a clear and peaceful [reign], a hero in a time of chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao refused until Cao cornered him; at last he said: "Under good government you would be a rogue; in chaos you are a hero.

sentences.zh: 」操大恱而去。

translations.literal: "Cao was greatly pleased and departed.
translations.idiomatic: "Cao Cao left well pleased.

sentences.zh: 劭從祖敬，敬子訓，訓子相，並爲三公，相以能諂事宦官，故自致台司封侯，數遣請劭。

translations.literal: Shao's great-uncle Jing, Jing's son Xun, Xun's son Xiang—all were Three Ducal Ministers; Xiang, because he was able to flatter and serve the eunuchs, therefore reached the high offices and was enfeoffed as marquis, and repeatedly sent to invite Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao's kinsmen Xu Jing, Xu Xun, and Xu Xiang had all reached the three highest posts; Xu Xiang had curried favor with the eunuchs to get there and repeatedly summoned Xu Shao to court.

sentences.zh: 劭惡其薄行，終不候之。

translations.literal: Shao detested his base conduct and to the end did not visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao despised his conduct and never answered the invitations.

sentences.zh: 劭邑人李逵，壯直有高氣，劭初善之，而後爲隙，又與從兄靖不睦，

translations.literal: Li Kui of Shao's district was stalwart, upright, and high-spirited; Shao at first was friendly with him, but later they had a rift; moreover he was not on good terms with his elder cousin Jing,
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, a fellow townsman, was blunt and proud—Xu Shao befriended him, then fell out; he also quarreled with his cousin Xu Jing—

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀志》曰：「許靖字文休，少與從弟劭俱知名，並有人倫臧否之稱，而私情不協。

translations.literal: (The Shu zhi says: "Xu Jing, style name Wenxiu, in youth was equally well known with his younger cousin Shao, and both had the reputation of judging human relations for good or ill, but their private feelings were not in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: (The Records of Shu: Xu Jing and his cousin were both famous talent-spotters but privately at odds—

sentences.zh: 劭爲郡功曹，排擯靖不得齒敘，以馬磨自給。」〉

translations.literal: When Shao was merit assessor of the commandery, he excluded Jing from being ranked in order, and [Jing] ground horse-mill to support himself.")
translations.idiomatic: when Xu Shao became merit assessor he struck Xu Jing from the rolls, leaving him to earn a living at a horse mill.")

sentences.zh: 時議以此少之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion on this account thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion faulted Xu Shao for pettiness.

sentences.zh: 初，劭與靖俱有高名，好共覈論鄉黨人物，每月輒更其品題，故汝南俗有「月旦評」焉。

translations.literal: At first Shao and Jing both had high reputations; they loved together to discuss critically the men of their village and district, each month changing their appraisals—therefore in Runan custom there was the "first-of-month judgment".
translations.idiomatic: The cousins had once shared fame for monthly rankings of local men—the "Yuedan" verdicts that gave Runan its proverbial "monthly critique."

sentences.zh: 司空楊彪辟，舉方正、敦樸，徵，皆不就。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yang Biao summoned him; he was recommended as upright, honest, and plain; he was summoned by imperial edict—he did not go to any.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned Minister Yang Biao, the recommendations for upright and plain virtue, and imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 或勸劭仕，對曰：「方今小人道長，王室將亂，吾欲避地淮海，以全老幼。

translations.literal: Someone urged Shao to take office; he replied: "Just now the way of petty men is growing; the royal house is about to be in chaos; I wish to flee the land to the Huai and sea, in order to preserve old and young.
translations.idiomatic: When urged to serve, he said: "Petty men are ascendant; the court will soon convulse. I mean to take my family to safety between the Huai and the sea.

sentences.zh: 」乃南到廣陵。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he went south to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: "He fled south to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史陶謙禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: Inspector of Xuzhou Tao Qian treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tao Qian of Xuzhou honored him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 劭不自安，告其徒曰：「陶恭祖外慕聲名，內非真正。

translations.literal: Shao was not at ease within; he told his followers: "Tao Gongzu outwardly admires reputation and fame; inwardly he is not genuine.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao mistrusted him and told his followers: "Tao Qian courts fame but lacks substance.

sentences.zh: 待吾雖厚，其埶必薄。

translations.literal: Although he treats me generously, his favor in the end will prove thin.
translations.idiomatic: His hospitality will not last.

sentences.zh: 不如去之。

translations.literal: It is better to leave him.
translations.idiomatic: We should leave.

sentences.zh: 」遂復投揚州刺史劉繇於曲阿。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he again attached himself to Inspector of Yang province Liu Yao at Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: "They joined Liu Yao, the Yangzhou inspector, at Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 〈繇字正禮。〉

translations.literal: (Yao's style name is Zhengli.)
translations.idiomatic: (Liu Yao, courtesy Zhengli.)

sentences.zh: 其後陶謙果捕諸寓士。

translations.literal: Afterwards Tao Qian indeed arrested the various sojourning scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian soon rounded up refugee scholars as Xu Shao had feared.

sentences.zh: 〈寓，寄也。〉

translations.literal: (Yu means to lodge.)
translations.idiomatic: (Yu: sojourning, lodging.)

sentences.zh: 及孫策平吳，劭與繇南奔豫章而卒，時年四十六。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce pacified Wu, Shao and Yao fled south to Yuzhang and died; he was forty-six years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce conquered Wu, Xu Shao fled with Liu Yao to Yuzhang and died there at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 兄虔亦知名，汝南人稱平輿淵有二龍焉。

translations.literal: His elder brother Qian was also well known; Runan people said that in the abyss of Pingyu there were two dragons.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xu Qian was equally celebrated—locals spoke of "two dragons in the Pingyu pool."

sentences.zh: 〈平輿故城，今豫州汝陽縣東北，有二龍鄉、月旦里。〉

translations.literal: (The old city of Pingyu is northeast of present-day Ruyang county in Yuzhou; there are Two-Dragon township and First-of-Month hamlet.)
translations.idiomatic: (The old Pingyu site lies northeast of Ruyang—local names still recall the two dragons and the monthly judgments.)

sentences.zh: 贊曰：林宗懷寶，識深甄藻。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Linzong cherished the jewel [within]; his discernment was deep in sorting and adorning.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Guo Tai bore his gifts inwardly and judged men with a jeweler's eye.

sentences.zh: 〈甄，明也。

translations.literal: (Zhen means to make clear.
translations.idiomatic: (Zhen here means to discriminate and clarify—

sentences.zh: 藻猶飾也。〉

translations.literal: Zao is glossed as adorning.)
translations.idiomatic: Zao suggests polish or adornment.)

sentences.zh: 明發周流，永言時道。

translations.literal: From dawn's light he circulated everywhere, ever speaking of the way of the times.
translations.idiomatic: He roamed from dawn to dusk, ever true to the temper of his age.

sentences.zh: 〈明發，發夕至明也。

translations.literal: (Mingfa: from dusk one is wakeful until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: (The phrase mingfa refers to rising from nightfall to dawn—

sentences.zh: 《呂氏春秋》曰：「孔子周流天下。」〉

translations.literal: The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Confucius circulated throughout the world.")
translations.idiomatic: as Confucius "circled the realm" in the Lüshi Chunqiu.)

sentences.zh: 符融鑒真，子將人倫。

translations.literal: Fu Rong mirrored truth; Zijiang [judged] human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong saw through pretense; Xu Shao set the measure of men.

sentences.zh: 守節好恥，並亦逡巡。

translations.literal: They guarded integrity and loved shame [i.e., sense of honor]; both also hesitated and held back.
translations.idiomatic: Both prized integrity and honor—and both stepped back from office.

sentences.zh: 〈逡巡，自退不仕也。〉

translations.literal: (Qunxun means to withdraw of oneself and not take office.)
translations.idiomatic: (Qunxun: to decline appointment, to hold aloof.)

translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianqian notes Huang Xian's biography uses gui-lan for the spring imagery (gui and lan springs).

translations.idiomatic: Collation: p. 2228, line 4—supplement "Zheng's Si Hong" in the Zuo Zhuan quotation.

translations.idiomatic: The commentary dropped "Zheng's Si Hong"; the line is restored from the received Zuo Zhuan.

translations.idiomatic: Collation: p. 2228, line 8, Sima Tang's remonstrance.

translations.idiomatic: Liu Congchen notes the Xin Xu reads Sima Tangju instead of Sima Tang.

translations.idiomatic: Collation: p. 2228, line 13, Mao Rong's courtesy name.

translations.literal: Liu Congchen says the Fengsu Tong has Mao Jiwei as a disciple of Huang Qiong—that is this man.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congchen identifies him with Mao Jiwei, pupil of Huang Qiong, in the Fengsu Tong.
